parameters.content:
## Hiring approvals: contract and signature
After the **last approval** the database writes the contract; **HR releases it** (one click in the Werkbank, never this workflow). Every 15 minutes this asks the database **what is due** (`recruiting_hire_contract_due`) and carries it out:
**prepare** the contract text (the database writes it from the approved terms), **ask** HR to release it (once), **send** the released contract to the e-signature service and record the envelope, **expire** a contract that stayed unsigned, and **tell** the requester (and HR after a signature) what came out.
The candidate's answer arrives at the webhook `hiring-contract-signature`; it is written back (`recruiting_hire_contract_result`) and the **signed document is stored in the database** with its hash. The database checks the envelope, the hash and the times; this workflow can neither approve a request nor change an approval.
**No e-signature service connected?** Leave `ESIGN_SEND_URL` empty: the workflow then runs a clearly labelled SIMULATION (envelope `SIM-<id>`, a signed text file that says it is a simulation, method `simulation`). It is not a legal signature.
**Setup:** environment variables `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` (service role key), `HIRING_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL`; for a real service `ESIGN_SEND_URL`, `ESIGN_API_KEY`, `ESIGN_PROVIDER`, `ESIGN_CALLBACK_URL` (the URL of the webhook below), `ESIGN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN` (the service sends it in the header `x-esign-token`), optional `ESIGN_VALID_DAYS` (14). n8n must allow `$env` in expressions (`N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false`). Apply migration 033 first. The send URL is an adapter you own: it receives `reference`, `candidate` (pseudonym), `document`, `sha256`, `start_on`, `callback_url`, looks up the signer in the recruiting system (the Werkbank holds no names or addresses) and answers `{ envelope, reference }`. Its callback sends `{ request, envelope, event: signed|declined|expired, signed_at, document_base64, sha256, method, reference }`.

parameters.jsCode:
// What goes to the e-signature service: the contract text and its hash, the pseudonym of the candidate and the start date. No name, no address, no amount.
return $input.all().map(({ json: d }) => ({ json: { id: d.id, payload: { reference: `HIRE-${d.id}`, candidate: d.candidate, title: d.title, document: d.body, sha256: d.bodySha256, start_on: d.startOn, callback_url: $env.ESIGN_CALLBACK_URL || '' } } }));

// The service answers with the envelope and echoes our reference (HIRE-<id>).
return $input.all().map(({ json }) => ({ json: { id: Number(String(json.reference || '').replace(/^HIRE-/, '')), envelope: String(json.envelope || ''), provider: $env.ESIGN_PROVIDER || 'e-signature service' } })).filter(({ json }) => Number.isInteger(json.id) && json.id > 0 && json.envelope);

// A contract the service did not accept stays 'prepared', so the next run tries again. This only lists them.
return [{ json: { failed: $input.all().length, items: $input.all().map(({ json }) => json.error?.message || 'send failed') } }];

// SIMULATION: no e-signature service is connected (ESIGN_SEND_URL is empty).
return $input.all().map(({ json: d }) => ({ json: { id: d.id, envelope: `SIM-${d.id}`, provider: 'simulation' } }));

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_id: $json.id, p_provider: $json.provider, p_ref: $json.envelope, p_valid_days: Number($env.ESIGN_VALID_DAYS || 14) }) }}

parameters.jsCode:
// The validity ended without an answer: the database accepts 'expired' only after that moment.
return $input.all().map(({ json: d }) => ({ json: { authorised: true, p_id: d.id, p_ref: String(d.envelope || ''), p_result: 'expired', p_signed_at: null, p_document: null, p_sha256: null, p_receipt: {} } }));

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ p_id: $json.p_id, p_ref: $json.p_ref, p_result: $json.p_result, p_signed_at: $json.p_signed_at, p_document: $json.p_document, p_sha256: $json.p_sha256, p_receipt: $json.p_receipt }) }}

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { accepted: true, status: $input.first().json.status, stored: $input.first().json.created === true } }];

// The database refused the answer (wrong envelope, hash that does not match, too early ...): nothing was changed.
return [{ json: { accepted: false, reason: $input.first().json.error?.message || 'refused' } }];
